grazzia.etymology: Inherited from Latin grātia. Cognate with Aragonese, Asturian, and Spanish gracia, Catalan gràcia, Portuguese graça, Old French grace, Piedmontese grassia and Corsican and Italian grazia.

panaru.etymology: Inherited from Latin pānārium, from pānis (“bread”) + -arium (“locative suffix”). Cognate with Italian paniere, Neapolitan panaro, Spanish panero.

du'.etymology: Apocopic form of dui, ultimately from Latin duo.

auricchia.etymology: From the riduction of Latin auricula, from auris (“ear”) + -cula (diminutive suffix). Cognate with Italian orecchia, Neapolitan aurecchia, Emilian uraccia, Catalan orella, Portuguese ourelha, Occitan aurelha and Spanish oreja.

aneḍḍu.etymology: From Latin anellus, diminutive of ānus (“anus, ring”). Compare Italian anello, Corsican, Sardinian, Gallurese, and Sassarese aneddu.

glosses_en: a male given name from Ancient Greek, equivalent to English Andrew
Annrìa.etymology: From Latin Andrīa, ultimately from Ancient Greek Ἀνδρέᾱς (Andréās, “courageous”). Compare Albanian Ndre, Serbo-Croatian Àndrija, Sardinian Andria and Italian Andrea.

nidu.etymology: From Latin nīdus, from Proto-Italic *nizdos (“nest”), from Proto-Indo-European *nisdós (“nest”).

casuḍḍa.etymology: From Late Latin casulla, formally from casul(a) + -(u)la, diminutive of Latin casa. By surface analysis, casa + -uḍḍa. Cognate with Catalan and Spanish casulla. Compare Italian casupola ~ casetta ~ casina.

glosses_en: any protruding body part, such as an overflowing belly
vaḍḍra.etymology: Likely from Arabic. Cognate with Neapolitan guàllara.

zuccru.etymology: From Arabic سُكَّر (sukkar). Compare Italian zucchero.

larunchia.etymology: This is to be considered one of the main variants borrowed from Gallo-Italic of Sicily. See the Doublet of ragrunchia for more.

glosses_en: sleep (viscous substance found in the corner of the eye after sleeping)
griḍḍu.etymology: Inherited from Latin gryllus (“cricket”). Compare Neapolitan grillo, arillo, Tarantino griḍḍi, and Italian grillo.

ragrunchia.etymology: Given the great amount of dialectal varieties, perhaps from an earlier metathetical dissimilated *ragruncula, from an unattested Vulgar Latin *grānucula, a diminutive from Latin rāna (“frog”) (with epenthetic ⟨g⟩); possibly influenced by th

mijolu.etymology: Through *mijiolu and *mujiolu, from Latin modiolus (“wheel hub”). Compare French moyeu.

glosses_en: courtyard surrounded by walls but open to the sky
curtigghiu.etymology: Likely from an earlier and unattested vulgar *cortiliu(m). By surface analysis, curti (“court”) + -igghiu. Compare Italian cortile (“courtyard”).

glosses_en: Untrue, not factual, factually incorrect; false.
Of a state in Boolean logic that indicates a negative result.
Not faithful or loyal, as to obligations, allegiance, vows, etc.; untrue; treacherous; sham.
Not well founded; not firm or trustworthy; erroneous.
fausu.etymology: From Latin falsus (perhaps influenced by an Occitan stratum), from fallere. Cognate with Italian falso.

cumparari.etymology: Semi-learned borrowing from Latin comparāre (“to compare, match, place together, couple”).

glosses_en: several species of juicy fruits or vegetables similar to watermelons, cucumbers or cucumis melo.
cucummru.etymology:
From an earlier cucumbru, probably through the intermediate of Old Occitan, as retained in
Old French cocombre. Possibily a wanderwort. More at Latin cucumis and Ancient Greek σῐκῠ́ᾱ (sĭkŭ́ā). Cognate with Italian cocomero.

fugazza.etymology: Likely Borrowed from Ligurian fogassa and/or Venetan fogassa; otherwise, in any case, from an Occitan stratum. Ultimately from Late Latin focācia, plural of focācium. Compare Italian focaccia.

glosses_en: A herb of the mint family, Origanum vulgare, having aromatic leaves.
Other herbs with a similar flavor, including other species in the genus Origanum, and Mexican oregano, Lippia graveolens.
The leaves of these plants used in flavouring food; oregano.
arrìganu.etymology: From Latin orīganum, from Ancient Greek ὀρίγανον (oríganon). Compare Italian origano.

glosses_en: alternative form of arrìganu and rìganu (apheretic variant)
rienu.etymology: Likely a dialectal stress shifted reduction of rìganu, collateral apheretic form of arrìganu.

glosses_en: a container, vase, or ampoule, traditionally made of terracotta
vùmmula.etymology: Uncertain. Supposedly derived from an earlier *bumbula ~ *bōmbola. Potentially derived from Byzantine Greek; possibly Greek βομβύλη (vomvýli, “vessel, vase, ampule”). Cognate with Italian bombola (“tank”).

glosses_en: A company (group, party, covey) of people, possibly that share the same interest or aim.

ḍḍu.etymology: From the intermediate *(i)llu, from Latin ille (“he, that”). Akin to iḍḍu (“he”) and collateral form of chiḍḍu (“that”). Compare also lu (“the or him/that”) ~ u (“the or him/that”).

chiḍḍa.etymology: From Latin (ec)cilla(m), contraction of eccum (“there she is”) + illa (“she, that”). Compare Corsican quella, Italian quella, Neapolitan chilla. Akin to iḍḍa and ḍḍa.

glosses_en: The name of the Latin script letter I/i.; i
i/languages M to Z.etymology: From Latin ī (the name of the letter I).

ḍḍa.etymology: From the intermediate *(i)lla, from Latin illa (“she, that”). Akin to iḍḍa (“she”) and collateral form of chiḍḍa (“that”). Compare also la (“the or her/that”) ~ a (“the or her/that”). Not to be confused with ḍḍà (“there”), nor dâ (“of the”)
